license_declaration.open_game_content: OGL 1.0a (Wizards of the Coast), inlined verbatim per docs/governance/ogl-pi-blacklist.md §2.2; the book's own _inner_sea_races.pcc declares ISOGL:YES (line 24) and carries a live COPYRIGHT block (lines 35-50, ending in 'Pathfinder Campaign Setting: Inner Sea Races Copyright 2015, Paizo Inc.') plus a real OGL.txt
license_declaration.product_identity_note: Named deities, nations, ethnicities and unique places of the Inner Sea region are Product Identity; the racial-trait rules text itself is Open Game Content. This is a campaign-setting book, so PI place and nation names occur inside otherwise-mechanical trait prose far more often than in a rulebook — 12 of this run's 72 records carry one and had their description field redacted rather than shipped.
license_declaration.product_identity_source: Paizo Pathfinder Campaign Setting: Inner Sea Races, OGL §15 Product Identity section

operator_sign_off.note: Set true only after an operator has reviewed this book's classification pass, per docs/governance/ogl-pi-blacklist.md's DRAFT header.

screening_method_note: Every field of the 72 alternate-racial-trait records this run wrote was screened against the bounded, documented term list in docs/governance/ogl-pi-blacklist.md by src/rules_core/pi_screening.rs, which the ingest binary calls per record. 12 descriptions hit a term and were replaced by the marker with pi_field recording which field was redacted; the record's mechanical payload (sets_replace_flags, raw_tokens, raw_bonus_chains) is untouched, so redaction costs prose and not rules. records_processed is 72, the real on-disk count for this book's only ingested kind. This is NOT an exhaustive human legal review; it is a bounded substring scan and does not prove the absence of PI beyond what that scan can see.
